literal: family, the people one provides for
usage: The general word for family in Modern Standard Arabic, covering parents, children and the wider relatives. usra is narrower and means the household you live with. Asking after someone's family is a normal part of greeting them.

variants.label: immediate family
variants.note: Use for parents and children living together; common in official language.

variants.label: one's people
variants.note: Warmer and broader: your people, your relatives.

variants.label: my family
variants.note: The form you need to talk about your own.

variants.label: family members
variants.note: Use when counting or listing relatives.

responses.english: I have a brother and a sister.

examples.english: I live with my family in Amman.
My family is the most important thing in my life.
